rv.q: An entertaining play, but it feels like Cameron lacked the patience to write a great one.

The Afronauts confirms his promise, and exudes a winning warmth. But despite beautiful vignettes evoking weightlessness and a canny harnessing of our collective imagination, rather like its subject it doesn't fully achieve lift-off.
Lucian Msamati anchors this ambitious, overstretched story of Afrofuturist ambition
It’s an interesting story that heads in many directions but ends up lost and atmosphere-less.
The Afronauts is a funny, bruising and beautifully realised play that earns its running time and then some.
It proves accessible, in places enlightening, and a surprisingly entertaining vehicle despite the deployment of a little historical licence and a slightly overlong first half.
Our problem with it is that it needs a good edit currently and to lose at least half an hour before the doubtless fascinating story at its heart can be emphasised with the clarity it deserves.

cn.t: Mixed reception for this ambitious true story of Zambia's 1960s space race. Stunning design and bold vision earn praise, but critics are divided on whether the drama fully launches — some soar with it, others feel it never quite lifts off.
